citation: Noh J, Kim Y, Lim C, et al.
title: Occupational and socioeconomic predictors of myocardial infarction and coronary heart disease: a machine learning analysis
population_and_data: Cross-sectional BRFSS 2023; 433,323 source respondents; reported MI/CHD prevalence about 8.47%.
outcome_definition: Prevalent self-reported MI or CHD (_MICHD); explicitly not prospective risk prediction.
predictors_and_methods: Logistic regression, decision tree, random forest and gradient boosting; inclusive and post-diagnosis-proxy-excluded model variants.
validation_design: 70:30 train/test split; five-fold stratified CV within training; hold-out test reserved for final evaluation.
reported_results: Gradient boosting ROC-AUC 0.867 and PR-AUC 0.389 in inclusive model; ROC-AUC 0.858 and PR-AUC 0.372 after proxy exclusions. Decision-tree variants were selected for subsequent analysis using prespecified sensitivity/specificity criteria.
calibration_and_threshold: Calibration curves, Brier score, calibration intercept/slope; model-specific threshold selection, held fixed for test evaluation.
survey_design_handling: Survey-weighted logistic-regression sensitivity analysis on complete-case subset n=40,073; ML models not weighted for full complex survey design.
limitations_and_comparability: Very close target/source-year comparator. Predictor panel and modeling decisions differ; metrics are not head-to-head. Cross-sectional reverse causation remains.
relevance_to_current_study: Establishes that BRFSS 2023 + prevalent MI/CHD classification and leakage-aware analysis are not novel by themselves. Supports framing our restricted six-predictor, frozen 2025 evaluation as a distinct applied design, not a first claim.
verification_status: Publisher full text reviewed 2026-10-25; methods and calibration sections checked.

citation: Kung WM, Yeh HC, Huang APH, Islam MM, Wu CC, Wang YC.
title: Machine Learning with Social Determinants of Health for Cross-Sectional Diabetes Classification: Development and Temporal Validation
population_and_data: BRFSS 2023 development cohort and BRFSS 2024 later-year sample.
predictors_and_methods: Nine classifiers, including penalized logistic regression and tree/boosting methods; social determinants of health considered.
validation_design: BRFSS 2023 development with internal holdout; frozen pipeline applied to BRFSS 2024 without refitting, retuning or threshold adjustment.
reported_results: Publisher search result confirms a BRFSS 2023 diabetes model was applied to BRFSS 2024 without refitting/retuning/threshold adjustment; detailed numerical results were not independently extracted in this pass.
calibration_and_threshold: Fixed threshold is described in the publisher result summary; exact threshold and full calibration metrics not independently extracted.
survey_design_handling: Article includes weighted metrics/analyses; full details should be extracted before citing specifics.
limitations_and_comparability: Different cross-sectional outcome (diabetes), so not a direct MI/CHD comparator. Full methods/results were not independently inspected line by line.
relevance_to_current_study: Important methodological analogue; narrows novelty to outcome-specific application and exact frozen six-feature MI/CHD specification.
verification_status: Publisher article page and indexed result reviewed 2026-10-25; direct full-page retrieval failed. Design is sufficiently clear to classify as a temporal-validation analogue; detailed numeric extraction remains unavailable.

citation: Wu B, Huang K, Hong X, Zhao SS, Yuan C, Li XG, et al.
title: Building and validating a machine learning model to predict coronary heart disease risk based on non-invasive indicators
venue: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine 275:109186
population_and_data: BRFSS development data and NHANES external-validation data; complete-case cohorts reported as BRFSS n=311,291 and NHANES n=5,674.
outcome_definition: CHD status described by the authors as risk prediction; exact outcome-code alignment with _MICHD requires full-text checking.
predictors_and_methods: Eight algorithms based on 12 clinical features; LightGBM selected; SHAP used for interpretation.
validation_design: Random 70:30 BRFSS split and external validation in NHANES.
reported_results: Abstract reports internal AUC 0.825 (95% CI 0.821–0.829) and external AUC 0.851 (95% CI 0.835–0.867).
calibration_and_threshold: Calibration details not established from the accessible abstract; thresholding details require full-text extraction.
survey_design_handling: Not established from the accessible abstract.
limitations_and_comparability: External validation uses a different survey, but outcome definition, eligibility and predictor set may differ from the present study. Abstract-only evidence is insufficient for direct numerical comparison.
relevance_to_current_study: Shows cross-survey external validation is already used in BRFSS-related CHD modeling; supports clear distinction between external NHANES validation and our later-year BRFSS evaluation.
verification_status: PubMed and publisher abstracts reviewed; full text not available in this review pass.

citation: Deng L, Lu K, Hu H.
title: An interpretable LightGBM model for predicting coronary heart disease: Enhancing clinical decision-making with machine learning
population_and_data: BRFSS 2015 used for model training; Framingham and Z-Alizadeh Sani datasets used for validation.
outcome_definition: CHD labels across three datasets; operational definitions and populations are not equivalent to current BRFSS _MICHD target.
predictors_and_methods: LightGBM; SHAP interpretation; feature engineering and missing-data handling.
reported_results: BRFSS AUROC about 0.811 after tuning; Framingham AUROC about 0.674 after tuning; metrics differ by dataset.
calibration_and_threshold: Calibration not established in the abstract sections reviewed; do not infer it from discrimination results.
survey_design_handling: Not described in the accessible article abstract.
limitations_and_comparability: Different years and datasets, with heterogeneous populations/outcome construction; not a direct comparator for 2023–2025 _MICHD.
relevance_to_current_study: Background for external transfer and interpretability; reinforces that different dataset AUCs are not head-to-head comparisons.

citation: Imani M, Maroosi A, Shojaei S, Heidari K, Hoseinzadeh SM, Daneshi N, et al.
title: Predicting cardiovascular diseases using imbalanced data: An XGBoost-based analysis of the 2022 BRFSS dataset
population_and_data: BRFSS 2022; article reports 445,132 original respondents and 221,643 included complete cases, but one results passage reports 12,884 positives + 209,039 negatives (total 221,923), which does not match 221,643.
outcome_definition: Binary self-reported CVD defined as affirmative response to either CHD or MI; related to _MICHD but the paper’s exact derived variable and codebook mapping should be checked.
predictors_and_methods: Thirteen demographic, chronic-condition, behavioral and social predictors; XGBoost, Random Forest, Logistic Regression and Naive Bayes; SMOTE applied to training data only according to Methods; SHAP interpretation.
validation_design: 80:20 stratified train/test split; stratified 10-fold CV and grid search on training data; test reportedly untouched by resampling/tuning.
reported_results: Abstract reports XGBoost accuracy 94.2%, F1 85.3%, ROC-AUC 0.94; Table 2 reports accuracy 85.02%, F1 85.34%, precision 83.43%, sensitivity 87.35%. The accuracy conflict and count mismatch (221,643 vs 221,923 when listed classes are summed) remain unresolved; do not use the disputed accuracy/AUC as a reliable comparative claim.
calibration_and_threshold: Calibration is not clearly reported in the accessible article text; no locked clinical threshold identified.
survey_design_handling: No survey-weighted model or design-based evaluation described in the abstract/methods reviewed.
limitations_and_comparability: Same BRFSS program and MI/CHD-related prevalent outcome, but uses 2022, 13 predictors, complete-case filtering and SMOTE. Internal sample-count and accuracy inconsistencies must be resolved; performance is not head-to-head.
relevance_to_current_study: Relevant comparator for BRFSS-based prevalent MI/CHD classification. The six-predictor 2023→2025 design differs, but generic target/model novelty cannot be claimed.
verification_status: PubMed/PMC/ScienceDirect accessible article text reviewed 2026-10-25; conflicting abstract/table metrics and sample counts recorded; no author clarification/code audit.

citation: Wanyonyi M, Morris ZN, Musyoka FM, Kitavi DM.
title: Enhanced machine learning and hybrid ensemble approaches for Coronary Heart Disease prediction
population_and_data: BRFSS-derived secondary dataset obtained via IEEE DataPort; article reports 253,680 records and 22 variables, 23,893 positive labels (9.42%); it then describes SMOTE expansion to 459,574 and a later Yamane-based subsample of about 9,789.
outcome_definition: Self-reported CHD/heart attack status in a secondary BRFSS-derived dataset; not the same annual source file or a verified exact match to the present project’s _MICHD processing.
predictors_and_methods: Hybrid/ensemble classifiers and clustering; SMOTE is described in the preprocessing section before the later train/validation/test split description; the actual code was not independently audited.
validation_design: Article describes 70% train / 15% validation / 15% test and five-fold CV during training. Since the written methods describe SMOTE and expansion before the split section, possible resampling leakage must be treated as a concern pending code/supplement verification, not as a confirmed error.
reported_results: Reported stacking ensemble accuracy 87.2%, sensitivity 89.6%, specificity 84.7%, AUC 0.94; HIRF AUC 0.937. These high metrics are not comparable to the locked project because of different source year, sample construction, class balancing and evaluation details.
calibration_and_threshold: Calibration curves reported for baseline and enhanced models; numeric calibration statistics and fixed-threshold details not extracted here.
survey_design_handling: No complex-survey design-based evaluation described in the passages reviewed; data are a secondary BRFSS-derived dataset rather than the original annual XPT.
limitations_and_comparability: Derived BRFSS dataset rather than direct analysis of current annual XPT; sample reduction and resampling sequence require clarification. Model AUCs are not comparable with the locked 2023/2025 pipeline.
relevance_to_current_study: Shows additional BRFSS-derived CHD classification work exists. It reinforces the need to distinguish the exact outcome/annual file and to avoid direct metric comparisons across differing resampling/evaluation procedures.
verification_status: PLOS ONE full-text methods/results/limitations reviewed 2026-10-25; resampling/split order is a text-based concern only; no code or supplemental implementation audit.

citation: Liu T, Krentz A, Lu L, Curcin V.
title: Machine learning based prediction models for cardiovascular disease risk using electronic health records data: systematic review and meta-analysis
population_and_data: Review of EHR-based CVD risk models for medium- to long-term (5–10 year) risk prediction; search covers 2010–2024.
outcome_definition: Incident/prognostic CVD risk in EHR studies, not prevalent self-reported BRFSS classification.
predictors_and_methods: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of ML and conventional risk models.
validation_design: Review of development and validation approaches across included studies.
reported_results: Abstract reports substantial heterogeneity (I² > 99%) and methodological concerns; pooled estimates are not comparable to current BRFSS metrics.
calibration_and_threshold: Calibration and risk-of-bias concerns discussed in review; detailed extraction not needed for direct performance comparison.
survey_design_handling: Not a complex-survey study; uses EHR evidence.
limitations_and_comparability: Different data sources and prospective outcome horizons. Search review should not be used to claim current BRFSS temporal validation is rare without a scope-matched search.
relevance_to_current_study: Supports separating cross-sectional classification from prospective cardiovascular-risk prediction and avoiding pooled cross-study AUC comparisons.
verification_status: PubMed and PMC full text reviewed 2026-10-25.

citation: Cai Y, Cai YQ, Tang LY, Wang YH, et al.
title: Artificial intelligence in the risk prediction models of cardiovascular disease and development of an independent validation screening tool: a systematic review
population_and_data: Systematic review searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase and IEEE to July 2021; 79 articles and 486 AI models included.
outcome_definition: Incident CVD risk prediction models; not cross-sectional _MICHD classification.
predictors_and_methods: Review using CHARMS and PROBAST; proposed independent validation score.
validation_design: Review of development/external validation; reported no independent external validations in the reviewed evidence through July 2021.
reported_results: All reviewed models were rated high risk of bias by PROBAST in this review; interpretation is limited to the review’s search period and included studies.
calibration_and_threshold: Reporting of performance and validation evaluated across studies.
survey_design_handling: Not focused on complex survey design.
limitations_and_comparability: Evidence base stops at July 2021 and cannot describe the full 2022–2026 landscape. It excludes pure outcome-classification studies, so it is context rather than a direct comparator.
relevance_to_current_study: Supports the need for transparent evaluation and independent validation, but not a contemporary novelty claim.

citation: Collins GS, Moons KGM, Dhiman P, Riley RD, et al.
title: TRIPOD+AI statement: updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods
predictors_and_methods: 27-item reporting checklist for prediction-model studies using regression or ML; includes subgroup performance, open-science and transparent methods reporting.
validation_design: Applies to model development and evaluation reporting.
calibration_and_threshold: Use to ensure discrimination, calibration, threshold and evaluation details are transparently reported where applicable.
survey_design_handling: Does not replace survey-specific design-based methods.
limitations_and_comparability: Reporting guidance is not a risk-of-bias rating tool and does not prescribe a modelling method. This project is a survey classifier, not a clinical prognostic tool; apply relevant items with scope caveat.
relevance_to_current_study: Use as a manuscript completeness checklist; do not claim compliance until an item-by-item audit is performed.
verification_status: BMJ full text and checklist scope reviewed 2026-10-25.

citation: Moons KGM, Damen JA, Kaul T, Hooft L, et al.
title: PROBAST+AI: an updated quality, risk of bias, and applicability assessment tool for prediction models using regression or artificial intelligence methods
predictors_and_methods: Updated tool with separate model-development and model-evaluation parts; domains include participants/data, predictors, outcome and analysis.
validation_design: Appraisal framework for development and evaluation studies.
calibration_and_threshold: Use to appraise calibration and evaluation methodology as part of the analysis domain.
survey_design_handling: Not a survey-specific framework; add survey design as a study-specific appraisal issue.
limitations_and_comparability: A formal PROBAST+AI rating has not yet been performed for this project; do not state a risk-of-bias grade without completing it.
relevance_to_current_study: Potential structured appraisal lens for comparator studies and our manuscript.

citation: Oh Y, Zheng HW, Feng J, Bui AAT.
title: Survey-Aware Machine Learning: A Guideline for Valid Population Health Inference based on Scoping Review
population_and_data: Scoping review of 16 methodological papers on complex health-survey ML, especially NHANES.
predictors_and_methods: Nine-step survey-aware ML guidance; covers weights, PSU, stratification, design-based validation and survey-adjusted evaluation.
reported_results: Identifies methodological gaps in weighted training, design-based CV, survey-adjusted performance, hyperparameter tuning and deployment.
calibration_and_threshold: Relevance depends on intended estimand and deployment use.
survey_design_handling: Central focus: survey design should be considered throughout the ML lifecycle rather than treating weights as a generic optional add-on.
limitations_and_comparability: Current project reports weighted evaluation point estimates only and does not provide full design-corrected uncertainty; explicitly frame them as sensitivity estimates, not valid complex-survey inference.
relevance_to_current_study: Critical limitation/positioning source. It may motivate a future separately designed survey-aware study, but must not trigger retroactive changes to locked Phase 1 results.
verification_status: PMLR full article landing page and abstract reviewed 2026-10-25.

citation: Steyerberg EW, Vickers AJ, Cook NR, Gerds T, et al.
title: Assessing the performance of prediction models: a framework for traditional and novel measures
population_and_data: Methodological paper with an illustrative external-validation example.
predictors_and_methods: Framework for discrimination, calibration, Brier score and decision-analytic metrics.
reported_results: Recommends reporting discrimination and calibration; decision analysis is needed if model is intended to guide clinical decisions.
calibration_and_threshold: Foundational justification for separately reporting discrimination, calibration and overall probability performance.
limitations_and_comparability: Foundational rather than contemporary BRFSS evidence.
relevance_to_current_study: Supports current reporting of ROC-AUC, Brier score and calibration diagnostics; does not imply clinical utility.

citation: Van Calster B, McLernon DJ, van Smeden M, Wynants L, Steyerberg EW.
title: Calibration: the Achilles heel of predictive analytics
calibration_and_threshold: Highlights calibration as distinct from discrimination and important to interpretation of predicted probabilities.
limitations_and_comparability: Existing seed records this source as reviewed; it was not re-opened during the current search session, so re-verify full bibliographic details before manuscript citation.
relevance_to_current_study: Useful conceptual background for interpreting cross-year Brier and calibration changes.
verification_status: Inherited from existing seed list; current-session re-verification pending.

title: Using broad health-related survey questions to predict the presence of coronary heart disease
population_and_data: BRFSS 2022; article reports over 300,000 survey samples.
outcome_definition: Binary classification of self-reported CHD and myocardial-infarction history; exact outcome code mapping should be checked before treating it as identical to _MICHD.
predictors_and_methods: Broad demographic, clinical and behavioral survey questions; coefficient-based interpretation; separate demographic-specific models also trained.
validation_design: 2022 BRFSS source had 445,132 rows; a preprocessed dataset of 340,200 rows was used. A 10% holdout (34,020) was reserved; the remaining 90% underwent stratified five-fold CV for model selection, with a logistic-regression model subsequently evaluated on the holdout.
reported_results: Global logistic-regression model: mean CV accuracy 0.725 and MCC 0.305; 10% holdout accuracy 0.724 and MCC 0.307. Abstract reports global MCC 0.299–0.313/accuracy 0.716–0.726 across binary classifiers; demographic-specific MCC up to 0.504.
calibration_and_threshold: Calibration and a fixed operating threshold were not reported in the examined methods/results. MCC was used alongside accuracy for class imbalance.
survey_design_handling: Complex survey weights were not reported in the examined analysis.
limitations_and_comparability: Same broad self-reported CHD/MI history family, but 2022 data, a larger and differently selected feature set, and different validation and metrics. Authors note demographic imbalance and possible self-report misclassification.
relevance_to_current_study: Another BRFSS-based study classifies self-reported CHD/MI history using broad survey variables, so outcome family and survey-data classification are not new. It is not a same-protocol comparison.
verification_status: Full 9-page journal PDF reviewed 2026-10-25; methods, results and limitations extracted. Exact outcome variable name/code mapping to current _MICHD was not independently confirmed.
